One_Body_Too_Many: One Body Too Many is a 1944 American comedy horror mystery film directed by Frank McDonald, starring Bela Lugosi, Jack Haley and Lyle Talbot. All we need is a thunderstorm. Aha! There it is now! Jean Parker is the damsel in peril. The ubiquitous Lyle Talbot is on hand in a supporting role. This one is fun. Bela again plays the role he was born for: cheerful yet sinister, and we are unsure if he is good or bad or both. rv: Lovely MOS scenic footage highlights this short, along with the bubbly narration of Art Gilmore. Plenty of shots of diesel-engine Santa Fe trains and a few nice shots of 19th century steam locomotives. The film is a well-written commercial with a little sub-plot about two children (the boy is wearing a suit and bow tie) on a thousand-mile trip. Railroads pay taxes, you know. As if other businesses don't, Editing is plentiful to hold interest and sound effects are well-chosen. A fine Dudley production. Oh, and there's plenty of flag-waving at the beginning and end. America's the greatest, you…

At 6:25 mark, workers with possible dirty hands are loading UNWRAPPED raw meat meant for human consumption. Appears meat was cross contaminated in an unrefrigerated box? My goodness, back in the days before plastic gloves and health codes. What was with the ending: "Railroads pay taxes for schools?" Most scenes appeared to be college footage, not public schools. Propaganda, silly script, and bad graphics places this up there with the classic "Duck & Cover." Thanks to the person who saved this treasure.
